Class A Common Stock
825,000,000 Shares
Anthropic, PBC
This is an initial public offering of shares of Class A common stock of Anthropic, PBC. We are selling 801,351,354 shares of Class A common stock and the selling
stockholders identified in this prospectus are selling an additional 23,648,646 shares of Class A common stock. We will not receive any proceeds from the sale of
shares of our Class A common stock by any of the selling stockholders.
Prior to this offering, there has been no public market for our Class A common stock. It is currently estimated that the initial public offering price per share will be
between $70.00 and $78.00. We have applied to list our Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.”
We have a novel capital and corporate governance structure. We are incorporated as a public benefit corporation under Delaware law, a structure consistent with our
commitment to artificial intelligence (“AI”) safety and responsibility. As a public benefit corporation, we are required to balance the pecuniary interests of our
stockholders, the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct, and the specific public benefit purpose identified in our amended and restated certificate of
incorporation: the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. We created our Long-Term Benefit Trust (the
“LTBT”) to help ensure that Anthropic, PBC is managed in a manner that responsibly balances its goals as a public benefit corporation. The LTBT is intended to
operate as an independent body of financially disinterested trustees with expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise. Through a special
class of common stock, Class T common stock, the LTBT generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who together will constitute a majority
of the authorized members of our board of directors. Our Class T common stock does not otherwise have voting rights with respect to matters submitted to
stockholders generally and has no economic rights. Immediately prior to the completion of this offering, we will also issue a single share of Class F common stock, a
special class of our common stock, to a limited liability company organized by our co-founders (the “Founder LLC”). Dario Amodei, our Chief Executive Officer and a
member of our board of directors, and Daniela Amodei, our President and Chairperson of our board of directors, together with our five other co-founders, will initially
be the sole members of the Founder LLC. Our Class F common stock, which will be held by the Founder LLC, will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that
equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of
our directors other than the Class T directors. Our Class F common stock will not have any economic rights. Immediately prior to the completion of this offering, we
will also authorize a special class of our common stock, Class E common stock, which will be issued to our employees, excluding our co-founders. Our Class E common
stock will be entitled to vote only on certain limited matters and will not have any economic rights. In addition, we have authorized Class A common stock and Class N
common stock. The rights of the holders of Class A common stock and Class N common stock are identical, except with respect to voting and conversion. Each share of
Class A common stock is entitled to one vote and shares of Class N common stock have no voting rights, except as otherwise required by law. The holders of our Class
N common stock are primarily strategic business partners, and shares of Class N common stock will generally convert to Class A common stock upon a sale or transfer
to an unaffiliated third party. Our Class A common stock is not convertible. See the sections titled “Risk Factors—Risks Related to our Governance Structure,” “Our
Governance Structure and Its Goals,” and “Description of Capital Stock” for more information.
We are considered a “controlled company” within the meaning of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements. See the sections titled “Our
Governance Structure and Its Goals,” “Management,” and “Description of Capital Stock” for additional information.
See the section titled “Risk Factors” beginning on page 29 to read about factors you should consider before buying shares of our Class
A common stock.

Select Defined Terms
The following are abbreviations, acronyms, and definitions of certain terms used in this prospectus:
“accelerators” refer to processors purpose-built or adapted for the large-scale computations required to pre-
train, post-train, refine, and run super intelligence models. These processors are significantly more efficient and
faster than general-purpose processors for these workloads.
“agent loop” refers to the iterative cycle in which an SI agent receives a task, takes an action, such as planning
a project, running code, or calling a tool, observes the result, and decides its next step, with this cycle repeating
until the task is complete. The agent loop is the core execution pattern underlying agentic SI behavior.
“agentic AI” or “agentic SI” refers to systems that, with varying degrees of autonomy, can plan, determine,
and sequence actions and execute them to accomplish defined objectives, including through interaction with
external tools, services, datasets, and environments on behalf of a user.
“API” refers to application programming interface, a standardized interface that allows external software to
access a system’s capabilities programmatically. SI model providers may offer APIs that allow software
developers to send inputs to a model and receive outputs, enabling integration into the software developers’
products and workflows.
“Applied AI” refers to a discipline and organizational function focused on embedding SI capabilities directly
into production business environments to address specific customer requirements. Applied AI teams, which
include forward-deployed engineers, work with enterprises to design and deploy custom solutions, specialized
workflows, and domain-specific implementations tailored to a customer’s own systems and processes.
“artificial intelligence” or “AI” refers to a machine-based system that learns or is trained from data and, for
explicit or implicit objectives and with varying levels of autonomy, processes that data to infer patterns,
generate outputs—such as predictions, content, recommendations, and decisions—and act upon physical or
virtual environments. For purposes of this prospectus, we use the terms “artificial intelligence,” “AI,” “super
intelligence,” and “SI” interchangeably.
“closing the loop” refers to a development cycle in which successive versions of an SI model assist in building
the next, with the goal of compounding capability gains over time.
“compute” refers to the computational processing resources used to train and run SI models, including,
without limitation, specialized accelerators, memory, networking, storage, and power systems that are deployed
in data centers or other physical computing environments.
“compute multipliers” refer to algorithmic and methodological improvements in training and inference that
increase the effective output of a given amount of compute.
“computer use” refers to an SI capability that allows a model to observe and interact with a graphical user
interface, such as clicking, typing, and navigating applications, similar to how a human operator would.
“Constitutional AI” refers to an approach to training AI models using a set of written principles, which we
refer to as Claude’s constitution, currently organized around four priorities: being broadly safe, broadly ethical,
compliant with our guidelines, and genuinely helpful. Under Constitutional AI, our models evaluate, critique,
and revise their own responses against these principles, enabling us to define and control model behavior
through auditable principles, rather than relying solely on fixed rule-based instructions or human reviewers.
“context window” refers to the maximum amount of text, code, or other content, measured in tokens, that an
SI model can process in a given request, encompassing instructions, prior conversation history, user input, and
the model’s output.
“CSP” refers to a cloud service provider, a technology company that owns and operates large-scale cloud
computing infrastructure and provides on-demand compute, storage, and networking. CSPs may also serve as
distribution channels through which SI products and services are made available to customers. The largest
2
Table of Contents
CSPs, sometimes referred to as hyperscalers, operate at global scale with significant infrastructure and market
concentration.
“customer” refers to a prosumer or an organization that uses our models, platform, or applications.
“customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis,” “customers with $1 million or
more of revenue on a TTM basis,” and “customers with $10 million or more of revenue on a TTM
basis” each refer to customers contributing revenue equal to or greater than the applicable dollar amount
during the trailing twelve-month (“TTM”) period ending on the measurement date. For purposes of this metric,
we define a customer as a distinct organization, identified by aggregating the accounts that we determine
belong to the same organization based on internal records and available data. We do not separately define or
internally track a category of “enterprise” customers, and our customers are not segmented or measured
internally by reference to whether a given customer is an “enterprise.” Because spending $100,000 or more on
our products is generally characteristic of organizational rather than individual usage, we use the number of
and revenue from customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis as our measure of enterprise
adoption and engagement with Claude throughout this prospectus, including in references to “enterprise
customers” and “enterprise adoption.”
“frontier intelligence” refers to SI systems at the current leading edge of capability and safety, performing at
or near the highest levels of any existing system across a broad range of tasks.
“hallucinations” refer to outputs in which an SI model generates factually incorrect or fabricated information
with apparent confidence.
“inference” refers to the process by which a trained SI model processes an input and generates an output.
Inference occurs each time a user or agent interacts with an SI system.
“interleaved thinking” refers to a capability whereby an SI model interposes discrete reasoning steps
between successive tool calls within a single response, rather than confining its reasoning to a single planning
phase at the outset.
“interpretability” refers to research into how and why SI models produce specific outputs, with the goal of
making model behavior more transparent and verifiable, especially in high-stakes applications.
“knowledge work” refers to complex cognitive work and related professional activities, including obtaining,
producing, analyzing, and communicating information through tasks such as coding, drafting analyses,
synthesizing research, building financial models, and managing and automating documents and workflows.
“LLMs” refer to large language models, or SI models trained primarily on large datasets to understand and
generate natural language and computer code.
“mechanistic interpretability” refers to a subfield of interpretability research focused on reverse-
engineering the internal computations of neural networks. Rather than inferring model behavior from inputs
and outputs alone, mechanistic interpretability seeks to identify the specific features and circuits within a model
that give rise to its behavior with the goal of making model reasoning auditable at the mechanism level and
detecting failure modes, including deceptive or unsafe behavior, that may not surface in standard testing.
“model weights” refer to the numerical parameters encoding a trained SI model’s behavior, which are the
primary intellectual asset of a frontier intelligence developer, representing the accumulated investment in
compute, data, and research.
“multi-agent orchestration” refers to an architecture in which multiple SI agents collaborate on a shared
task, with one coordinating while others execute subtasks in parallel, enabling more complex, long-horizon
work than a single agent can complete alone.
“Net Revenue Retention” reflects customer expansion, contraction, and churn as of a measurement date.
We calculate Net Revenue Retention by dividing the Qualified Customers’ Current Period revenue by their Base
Period revenue. A Qualified Customer is a customer with at least $1 of revenue during the Base Period,
excluding subscribers to our Claude Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, whose fixed-price subscriptions do not reflect
3
Table of Contents
the expansion and contraction behavior this metric is intended to capture. The Base Period is the three months
ending a year prior to the measurement date. The Current Period is the three months ending as of the
measurement date.
“open-weight” refers to an SI model whose trained model weights are publicly released, allowing third parties
to download, run, and modify the model, subject to the terms of the model’s license, without necessarily
providing access to the underlying training data or code.
“pay-for-intelligence” or “consumption” refers to our revenue model under which customers pay for their
usage of our intelligence service, which is metered in tokens and priced according to the model selected.
“persistent,” in the context of SI applications, refers to denoting data, state, or context that is continuously
retained beyond the boundary of a single operation, session, or interaction, remaining accessible for reuse
across subsequent steps, sessions, or workflows without requiring reinitialization.
“post-training” refers to the collection of techniques applied to a pre-trained model to refine its behavior,
including reinforcement learning, supervised refinement methods, and other alignment methods. Post-training
is the stage in which much of the work to make a frontier model helpful, accurate, and safe is performed,
including the application of safety and alignment techniques.
“pre-training” refers to the initial stage of training an SI model, in which the model learns general patterns
and representations from large-scale datasets of text, code, and other data, typically by predicting the next
token in a sequence. The output of pre-training is a base model with broad capabilities that has not yet been
adapted for any specific deployment context.
“primitives” refer to the foundational, modular building blocks of a software system from which more
complex applications and workflows are constructed.
“prompt injection” refers to an adversarial technique in which malicious instructions are embedded in
content an SI model is asked to process, such as websites, documents, or tool outputs, with the aim of
overriding or manipulating the model’s intended behavior, typically without the user’s knowledge.
“prosumers” refer to individual users who subscribe to SI tools to perform knowledge work.
“reinforcement learning” refers to a machine learning approach in which a model learns to perform a task
by taking actions, receiving feedback signals called rewards, and adjusting its behavior to maximize the rewards
it accrues over time. In contemporary SI development, reinforcement learning is widely used to refine model
behavior after pre-training, including to improve helpfulness, accuracy, and adherence to safety guidelines.
“RLHF” refers to reinforcement learning from human feedback, a specific form of reinforcement learning in
which human evaluators rate the model’s responses, and those ratings are used as the reward signal to guide
training.
“Run-Rate Revenue” is an operating metric that refers to the estimated annualized value of our revenue-
generating activity as of a measurement date, calculated as the sum of (i) our consumption-based fees during
the trailing 28-day period ended on the measurement date, multiplied by 13, and (ii) our aggregate monthly
subscription fees as of the measurement date, multiplied by 12. For purposes of calculating Run-Rate Revenue,
consumption-based fees and subscription-based fees are derived from customer usage and active subscriptions.
“super intelligence” or “SI” refers to a machine-based system that learns or is trained from data and, for
explicit or implicit objectives and with varying levels of autonomy, processes that data to infer patterns,
generate outputs—such as predictions, content, recommendations, and decisions—and act upon physical or
virtual environments. For purposes of this prospectus, to avoid confusion, we use the terms “super
intelligence,” “SI,” “artificial intelligence,” and “AI” interchangeably. On September 29, 2026, the President of
the United States issued Executive Order 14434, which directs federal executive departments and agencies to
use the terms “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in place of “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI.”
“systems integrators” refer to third-party technology and professional services firms that design, build, and
deploy integrated solutions for customers by combining products and services from multiple technology
vendors into unified systems tailored to customer needs.
4
Table of Contents
“tokens” refer to numeric units into which an SI model converts the data it processes, including text, images,
audio, and video, the number of which varies by the model and tokenizer applied. Tokens are the smallest
individual units of data a language model processes and can correspond to words, subwords, characters, or
bytes. A tokenizer is the component of a model that converts customer inputs into the sequence of tokens the
model processes and then converts the processed tokens into the outputs provided to customers.
1 For purposes of this prospectus, we use the terms “super intelligence,” “SI,” “artificial intelligence,” and “AI” interchangeably.

Overview
For the first time in history, intelligence is something humans can build. The cognitive capability to reason,
analyze, synthesize, decide, and create is producible at scale and accessible on demand. We believe this
abundance of super intelligence1 will rapidly transform every sector of the global economy in ways greater than
the impact of industrialization, electricity, semiconductors, and the internet. If this technology truly delivers on
its potential—with the risks well managed—it could significantly accelerate global growth and dramatically
improve quality of life for people around the world.
Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a team of researchers responsible for many of the breakthroughs that define
SI. We are first and foremost a research lab—our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of
advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. This mission directs our focus—along with our talent and
culture, our frontier and safety research, our approach to compute, and our enterprise strategy, it is one of the
core advantages that set us apart. These advantages enable us to continuously advance frontier intelligence and
shape the standards for its safe and responsible development. Our frontier intelligence, Claude, is delivered to
customers through our models, platform, and applications. Claude has experienced the fastest enterprise
adoption of any technology in history, as demonstrated by revenue growing from $0 at commercial launch in
the first quarter of 2023 to $17.0 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026. This rapid and
growing adoption generates two self-reinforcing dynamics—an improvement loop that advances Claude and an
investment loop that helps fund our continued research at the frontier.
Our Core Advantages
Mission & Focus. All of our efforts are guided by a singular focus on our mission. This focus enables us to
concentrate talent, research, and compute investment on the highest-value work for humanity and to avoid
conflicting priorities. Achieving our mission means the world gains the enormous benefits of frontier
intelligence while mitigating the most significant risks, and we believe this requires safety and capability to
advance together.
Talent & Culture. Our mission and focus enable us to attract and retain world-class talent, including
researchers and engineers who want their work to shape a better future. We also have a culture that promotes a
low-ego, truth-seeking environment, where frontier capability and safety are mutually reinforcing. We believe
our culture has driven our talent density as we have scaled.
Frontier & Safety Research. We believe that sustained, focused research at the frontier of intelligence is
required to build the most capable and safest super intelligence systems. Our frontier capabilities and safety
research are deeply integrated and directly shape model design, training, and deployment, helping us produce
systems that are more reliable, steerable, and well suited for real-world deployment, particularly in demanding
enterprise environments. We translate our research leadership into innovation velocity and have consistently
released better models, platform capabilities, and applications. Each version of a Claude model assists in
building the next, helping to compress development timelines and produce compounding improvements in the
